# OpenSSF Newsletter – June 2026 – Open Source Security Foundation

June highlighted the high stakes for open source security. The [European Open Source Security Forum](https://openssf.org/event/european-open-source-security-forum-2026/) focused on turning CRA commitments into action, while the Mini Shai-Hulud and Miasma threats underscored the need for strong provenance. Despite these challenges, the community progressed with new machine-readable guidance, a SLSA supply chain post-mortem, and a critical CRA Awareness report. Read on for the full update!

### TL;DR

- 📋 [2026 CRA Awareness & Readiness Report](https://openssf.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/2026_CRA_Awareness_Readiness_Report.pdf) → Two-thirds of the open source community still don’t know what the EU CRA requires — and the September deadline is approaching.
- 🎬 [OpenSSF Community Day NA Sessions Now on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=48qIJBtpm5A&list=PLVl2hFL_zAh-Dwjkj6nqXsA5EDY-fGSNG) → All session recordings from OpenSSF Community Day North America are live in a full playlist.
- 🔗 [Mini Shai-Hulud: Where SLSA’s Boundaries Fall](https://openssf.org/blog/2026/06/10/mini-shai-hulud-where-slsas-boundaries-fall/) → SLSA team publishes a clear-eyed breakdown of what the worm exploited, what the framework prevents, and what it can’t.
- 🔎 [Aligning on Machine-Readable Signals as the Foundation for Due Diligence](https://openssf.org/blog/2026/05/29/aligning-on-machine-readable-signals-as-the-foundation-for-due-diligence/) → Modern supply chains need automated signals, not manual checklists.
- 📦 [AMPEL Accepted as New Sandbox Project](https://github.com/ossf/tac/blob/main/process/project-lifecycle-documents/AMPEL_sandbox_stage.md) → New OpenSSF project makes supply chain security assertions practical, composable, and automatable.
- 🎙️ [Podcast: Mentorship & Community](https://openssf.org/podcast/) → This month’s episodes dive deeply into the impact of open source on the enterprise, exploring security and career growth with IBM’s Jamie Thomas while also tackling the hidden risks of end-of-life dependencies with HeroDevs.

## [The CFP for OpenSSF Community Day Europe 2026 is open through July 12, + Additional Track for SCORED Research Papers](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/openssf-community-day-europe/program/cfp/)

The Call for Proposals for OpenSSF Community Day Europe 2026 is open through Sunday, July 12 at 11:59 PM CEST.  The event occurs on October 6 in Prague, Czechia, co-located with Open Source Summit Europe. This year, we added the Software Supply Chain Offensive Research and Ecosystem Defenses (SCORED) conference as a new dedicated technical track, inviting researchers from academia to submit original research papers. [Register](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/openssf-community-day-europe/register/) | [Submit your talk](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/openssf-community-day-europe/program/cfp/) | [Sponsor](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/openssf-community-day-europe/sponsor/)

## [2026 CRA Awareness and Readiness Report](https://openssf.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/2026_CRA_Awareness_Readiness_Report.pdf)

The 2026 CRA Awareness and Readiness Report is live, and the findings are stark. Today, 66% of developers, manufacturers, and contributors worldwide are “not familiar at all” or “only slightly familiar” with the CRA, a number that rises to 72% in the US and Canada. [Download the report](https://openssf.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/2026_CRA_Awareness_Readiness_Report.pdf) and read CRob’s companion blog post, [Taking Stock of the State of European Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) Compliance: An Urgent Wake-up Call for the Open Source Ecosystem](https://openssf.org/blog/2026/05/18/taking-stock-of-the-state-of-european-cyber-resilience-act-cra-compliance-an-urgent-wake-up-call-for-the-open-source-ecosystem/) , for his direct assessment of what the data means.

## [The “Skyway” to OSS Security: OpenSSF Community Day North America 2026 Recap](https://openssf.org/blog/2026/06/05/the-skyway-to-oss-security-openssf-community-day-north-america-2026-recap/)

Missed Minneapolis? Catch up on everything you missed with our newly published recap of OpenSSF Community Day North America. The [complete YouTube session playlist](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=48qIJBtpm5A&list=PLVl2hFL_zAh-Dwjkj6nqXsA5EDY-fGSNG) is now live, featuring a broad security spectrum that spans from post-quantum readiness and AI-driven orchestration to deep dives into SBOM transparency and trusted publishing. [Read the recap](https://openssf.org/blog/2026/06/05/the-skyway-to-oss-security-openssf-community-day-north-america-2026-recap/) to explore the highlights and relive the day’s most impactful moments!

## [Mini Shai-Hulud: Where SLSA’s Boundaries Fall](https://openssf.org/blog/2026/06/10/mini-shai-hulud-where-slsas-boundaries-fall/)

On May 11, the Mini Shai-Hulud worm compromised 84 npm package artifacts across 42 TanStack packages and spread to 170+ packages across other ecosystems. The SLSA team published a thorough post-mortem: a signed attestation confirms what the build platform observed, not whether the build itself was trustworthy. [Read the full analysis](https://openssf.org/blog/2026/06/10/mini-shai-hulud-where-slsas-boundaries-fall/) for what the framework covers, what policy must close, and what operational controls teams can put in place today.

## [Aligning on Machine-Readable Signals as the Foundation for Due Diligence](https://openssf.org/blog/2026/05/29/aligning-on-machine-readable-signals-as-the-foundation-for-due-diligence/)

Software supply chains have grown too complex for manual compliance oversight. OpenSSF EU Policy Advisor Madalin Neag argues that the only scalable path forward is automated, machine-readable security signals – and that OpenSSF tooling like Security Insights, OSPS Baseline, and Gemara provide the building blocks both regulators and maintainers need. [Read the blog](https://openssf.org/blog/2026/05/29/aligning-on-machine-readable-signals-as-the-foundation-for-due-diligence/) .

## What’s in the SOSS? An OpenSSF Podcast

[#62 – S3E14 The Ghost in the Dependency Tree: Navigating Open Source End-of-Life with HeroDevs](https://openssf.org/podcast/2026/06/02/whats-in-the-soss-podcast-62-s3e14-the-ghost-in-the-dependency-tree-navigating-open-source-end-of-life-with-herodevs/)

CRob sits down with Isaac Wuest, Product Line Leader at HeroDevs, to explore the critical and often overlooked “gray area” of the software supply chain: End-of-Life (EOL) software. While the industry heavily relies on CVEs to track vulnerabilities, Isaac explains how maintainer abandonment creates a vacuum where risks are present but remain undiscovered and unreported. [Listen now](https://openssf.org/podcast/2026/06/02/whats-in-the-soss-podcast-62-s3e14-the-ghost-in-the-dependency-tree-navigating-open-source-end-of-life-with-herodevs/) .

[#63 – S3E15 Big Thoughts, Open Sources: Driving Enterprise Security and Career Growth Through Open Source with Jamie Thomas (IBM)](https://openssf.org/podcast/2026/06/16/whats-in-the-soss-podcast-63-s3e15-big-thoughts-open-sources-driving-enterprise-security-and-career-growth-through-open-source-with-jamie-thomas-ibm/)

Join CRob and Jamie Thomas, IBM Enterprise Security Executive and OpenSSF Governing Board Member (former Chair!), as they tackle the vital shifting dynamics of enterprise open source engagement. From IBM’s historical “billion-dollar bet” on Linux to modern supply chain wake-up calls like SolarWinds and Log4j, Jamie pulls back the curtain on what it truly means to move from accidental consumption to intentional stewardship. [Listen now](https://openssf.org/podcast/2026/06/16/whats-in-the-soss-podcast-63-s3e15-big-thoughts-open-sources-driving-enterprise-security-and-career-growth-through-open-source-with-jamie-thomas-ibm/) .

## News from OpenSSF Community Meetings and Projects

[Upcoming community meetings](https://openssf.org/calendar/)

- Generative AI is shifting how you use, build, and maintain open source software. The Linux Foundation, OpenSSF, LF AI & Data Foundation, and ActiveState launched a joint survey to map this changing AI security landscape, and we need your input. [Take the survey](https://linuxfoundation.research.net/r/KL58BBN) .
- On June 10, OpenSSF participated in the second [Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) Expert Group](https://ec.europa.eu/transparency/expert-groups-register/screen/expert-groups/consult?lang=en&groupID=3967) meeting of the year.
- If you missed our recent CRA Tech Talk on June 15th dedicated to upstream contributors, you can now catch up on the full recording [here](https://zoom.us/rec/play/mDn05ZJngwuBfM2cYoDe9Bd7kE1Hnv5BcTenwSWKxFgrBOYzQGyWFTxTg5WelpxXIwRoV7l74DUuJRUA.UlTakUhvy4nqwz8d?accessLevel=meeting&canPlayFromShare=true&from=share_recording_detail&continueMode=true&oldStyle=true&componentName=rec-play&originRequestUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fzoom.us%2Frec%2Fshare%2F433C9E67lEHD_wvLvRFDM0N2yX8geBy8fKKX6Ouw1CY90szWv1YRW2YwRqafJFd0.Ur7f0s0ABG3Vzst-) .
- [Videos for all sessions from OpenSSF Community Day North America](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=48qIJBtpm5A&list=PLVl2hFL_zAh-Dwjkj6nqXsA5EDY-fGSNG) are now available in a full playlist on YouTube. [OpenSSF @ Open Source Summit North America YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLSs2ZpvI7HaY&si=TCGms1Ssev71evNH) is also now available.
- [AMPEL was accepted as a new OpenSSF sandbox project](https://github.com/ossf/tac/blob/main/process/project-lifecycle-documents/AMPEL_sandbox_stage.md) by the TAC. The project’s mission is to make supply chain security assertions practical, composable, and automatable.
- OpenSSF is compiling a [literature search](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Q3zQ30uEAegSGZr8mlgmrO92fm_BmdozwKbPVoD-Tos/edit?tab=t.0) to develop an LF Education course on Using AI to Find and Fix Vulnerabilities in Open Source Software.
- OpenBao released [v2.5.4](https://github.com/openbao/openbao/releases/tag/v2.5.4) with patches for three CVEs, several bug fixes, and a PostgreSQL storage improvement.
- The [ORBIT Launchpad SIG](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HIe6ftj18YldRy55BsPbgTj0Za2duCck0W4dZAw1sGw/edit?tab=t.0) is working on a CRA Baseline for Open Source Consumption and a CRA Baseline for Manufacturers.
- Zarf released [v0.77](https://github.com/zarf-dev/zarf/releases/tag/v0.77.0) with keyless Sigstore signing support, the ability to pull images by index SHA, archive inclusion in image discovery, and a fix for the signing auth flow in CI environments.
- The Vulnerability Disclosures WG continues progress on [guidance for AI in vulnerability disclosure](https://github.com/ossf/wg-vulnerability-disclosures/issues/178#issuecomment-4671355906) .
- Gemara released [v1.2.0](https://github.com/gemaraproj/gemara/releases/tag/v1.2.0) with an optional rank field in the risk catalog for risk prioritization and maintenance updates.
- CFPs are open for [AGNTCon + MCPCon Japan](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/agntcon-mcpcon-japan/program/cfp/#overview) , [OpenSSF Community Day Europe](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/openssf-community-day-europe/program/cfp/) (closes July 12), and [Open Source Summit Europe](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/open-source-summit-europe/program/cfp/#overview) .

## Member Spotlight

**ActiveState – Free Certification: Open Source Software Security Management**

OpenSSF General Member ActiveState is offering a free, self-paced certification on open source risk management across the software supply chain — covering vulnerability detection and remediation, artifact management, and supply chain controls. Earn a shareable LinkedIn badge on completion. [Get started](https://www.activestate.com/academy/open-source-software-security-management/) .

**CleanStart – 100 Verified Container Images Milestone**

OpenSSF General Member CleanStart recently crossed the milestone of [100 CleanStart Verified container images](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/cleanstart-official_softwaresupplychain-containersecurity-devsecops-activity-7473236518036250626-IpJ4) , which is a meaningful marker for the software supply chain and container security community.

## In the News

- **Infosecurity Magazine:**[Two-Thirds of Open Source Community Unaware of Cyber Resilience Act](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/open-source-unaware-cyber/)
- **ITOps Times’ “Get with IT” Podcast:**[The Sustainability Gap in Open Source Package Repositories (CRob)](https://open.spotify.com/episode/3D0YxdsFV7uQyU2HcoDitF?si=kOnKkdQaSB27IMxttJfDNg)
- **Tech Times** : [EU Cyber Resilience Act: 24-Hour Vulnerability Clock Starts September 11 for IoT Vendors](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/318255/20260611/eu-cyber-resilience-act-24-hour-vulnerability-clock-starts-september-11-iot-vendors.htm)
- **TFiR** : [How to Prepare for EU Cyber Resilience Act Compliance Before Enforcement Hits | Christopher Robinson, OpenSSF | TFiR](https://tfir.io/eu-cyber-resilience-act-compliance-openssf/)
- **DevOps.com:**[OpenSSF’s CRob: ‘The Runway Is Rapidly Running Out’ on EU CRA Readiness](https://devops.com/openssfs-crob-the-runway-is-rapidly-running-out-on-eu-cra-readiness/)

## Meet OpenSSF at These Upcoming Events!

Connect with the OpenSSF Community at these key events:

- [Black Hat 2026](https://openssf.org/event/black-hat-2026/) – August 1–4, Las Vegas, NV
- [OpenSSF Community Day Europe 2026](https://openssf.org/event/openssf-community-day-europe-2026/) – October 6, Prague, Czechia
- [Open Source Summit Europe 2026](https://openssf.org/event/open-source-summit-europe-2/) – October 7–9, Prague, Czechia
- [All Things Open 2026](https://openssf.org/event/all-things-open/) – October 19–20, Edinburgh, UK
- [AGNTCon + MCPCon North America](https://openssf.org/event/agntcon-mcpcon-north-america/) – October 20–23, San Jose, CA
- [Open Source SecurityCon North America 2026](https://openssf.org/event/open-source-securitycon-north-america/) – November 9, Salt Lake City, UT
- [KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026](https://openssf.org/event/kubecon-cloudnativecon-north-america/) – November 9–12, Salt Lake City, UT

There are a number of ways for individuals and organizations to participate in OpenSSF. Learn more [here](https://openssf.org/getinvolved/) .

- Join a [Working Group](https://openssf.org/community/openssf-working-groups/) or [Project](https://openssf.org/projects/)
- Chat with us on [Slack](https://slack.openssf.org/)
- Follow us on [X](https://twitter.com/openssf) , [Mastodon](https://social.lfx.dev/@openssf) , Bluesky , and [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/openssf/)
- [Join OpenSSF](https://openssf.org/join/)

## See You Next Month!

### 重點摘要

- 📋 [2026 CRA 認知與準備度報告](https://openssf.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/2026_CRA_Awareness_Readiness_Report.pdf) → 三分之二的開源社群仍不知道歐盟 CRA 的要求，而 9 月期限正在逼近。
- 🎬 [OpenSSF Community Day 北美場次現已上架 YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=48qIJBtpm5A&list=PLVl2hFL_zAh-Dwjkj6nqXsA5EDY-fGSNG) → OpenSSF Community Day North America 的所有場次錄影都已整理成完整播放清單上線。
- 🔗 [Mini Shai-Hulud：SLSA 的邊界落在哪裡](https://openssf.org/blog/2026/06/10/mini-shai-hulud-where-slsas-boundaries-fall/) → SLSA 團隊發布了一份清晰務實的解析，說明這隻蠕蟲利用了什麼、這套框架能防止什麼，以及它無法防止什麼。
- 🔎 [把機器可讀訊號對齊為盡職調查的基礎](https://openssf.org/blog/2026/05/29/aligning-on-machine-readable-signals-as-the-foundation-for-due-diligence/) → 現代供應鏈需要自動化訊號，而不是手動檢查清單。
- 📦 [AMPEL 獲接受為新的 Sandbox 專案](https://github.com/ossf/tac/blob/main/process/project-lifecycle-documents/AMPEL_sandbox_stage.md) → 這個新的 OpenSSF 專案讓供應鏈安全聲明變得實用、可組合且可自動化。
- 🎙️ [Podcast：指導與社群](https://openssf.org/podcast/) → 本月節目深入探討開源對企業的影響，與 IBM 的 Jamie Thomas 一起討論安全與職涯成長，同時也處理 HeroDevs 提出的終止生命週期相依套件所隱藏的風險。

## [OpenSSF Community Day Europe 2026 徵稿開放至 7 月 12 日，並新增 SCORED 研究論文 Track](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/openssf-community-day-europe/program/cfp/)

OpenSSF Community Day Europe 2026 的徵稿提案（Call for Proposals）開放至歐洲中部夏令時間 7 月 12 日星期日晚上 11:59。活動將於 10 月 6 日在捷克布拉格舉行，並與 Open Source Summit Europe 同場舉辦。今年，我們新增了 Software Supply Chain Offensive Research and Ecosystem Defenses（SCORED，軟體供應鏈攻擊研究與生態系防禦）會議，作為專門的技術議程軌，邀請學術界研究人員提交原創研究論文。[報名](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/openssf-community-day-europe/register/) | [投稿你的演講](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/openssf-community-day-europe/program/cfp/) | [贊助](https://events.linuxfoundation.org/openssf-community-day-europe/sponsor/)

軟體供應鏈已經複雜到無法只靠人工進行法遵監督。OpenSSF 歐盟政策顧問 Madalin Neag 主張，唯一可規模化的前進方式，是自動化、機器可讀的安全訊號；而 Security Insights、OSPS Baseline、Gemara 等 OpenSSF 工具，正提供監管機關與維護者都需要的建構基礎。[閱讀部落格文章](https://openssf.org/blog/2026/05/29/aligning-on-machine-readable-signals-as-the-foundation-for-due-diligence/)。

## SOSS 裡有什麼？OpenSSF Podcast

[#62 – S3E14 依賴樹中的幽靈：與 HeroDevs 一起面對開源生命週期終止](https://openssf.org/podcast/2026/06/02/whats-in-the-soss-podcast-62-s3e14-the-ghost-in-the-dependency-tree-navigating-open-source-end-of-life-with-herodevs/)

CRob 與 HeroDevs 產品線負責人 Isaac Wuest 對談，探討軟體供應鏈中關鍵卻常被忽略的「灰色地帶」：生命週期終止（End-of-Life, EOL）軟體。雖然業界高度仰賴 CVE 來追蹤漏洞，Isaac 說明了維護者放棄維護如何形成真空，使風險已經存在，卻仍未被發現、也未被通報。[立即收聽](https://openssf.org/podcast/2026/06/02/whats-in-the-soss-podcast-62-s3e14-the-ghost-in-the-dependency-tree-navigating-open-source-end-of-life-with-herodevs/)。

[#63 – S3E15 大思考，開放來源：與 Jamie Thomas（IBM）談如何透過開源推動企業安全與職涯成長](https://openssf.org/podcast/2026/06/16/whats-in-the-soss-podcast-63-s3e15-big-thoughts-open-sources-driving-enterprise-security-and-career-growth-through-open-source-with-jamie-thomas-ibm/)

跟著 CRob 與 IBM 企業安全主管、OpenSSF 理事會成員 Jamie Thomas（前任主席！）一起討論企業參與開源時正在發生的重要變化。從 IBM 過去對 Linux 下的「十億美元賭注」，到 SolarWinds 與 Log4j 這類現代供應鏈警鐘，Jamie 揭開幕後，說明從偶然取用轉向有意識地承擔維護責任，真正意味著什麼。[立即收聽](https://openssf.org/podcast/2026/06/16/whats-in-the-soss-podcast-63-s3e15-big-thoughts-open-sources-driving-enterprise-security-and-career-growth-through-open-source-with-jamie-thomas-ibm/)。

## 會員焦點

**ActiveState – 免費認證：開源軟體安全管理**

OpenSSF 一般會員 ActiveState 提供一門免費、可自主安排進度的認證課程，內容涵蓋整個軟體供應鏈中的開源風險管理，包括漏洞偵測與修補、軟體構件管理，以及供應鏈控管。完成後可取得能分享到 LinkedIn 的徽章。[開始學習](https://www.activestate.com/academy/open-source-software-security-management/)。

**CleanStart – 達成 100 個經驗證容器映像檔里程碑**

OpenSSF 一般會員 CleanStart 最近跨越了 [100 個 CleanStart Verified 容器映像檔](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/cleanstart-official_softwaresupplychain-containersecurity-devsecops-activity-7473236518036250626-IpJ4) 的里程碑，對軟體供應鏈與容器安全社群來說，是一項有意義的指標。
